Whether you hit a patch of black ice, or your tires are frozen or worn out, everyone who drives in winter conditions is going to slide, whether you crash or not is really up to you and the other drivers around you.

Most important thing about winter driving is to be mindful of other drivers, you can't predict how other vehicles are going to act.

Most winter driving accidents are caused by sliding vehicles in one way or another. sliding into ditches or roadside objects, sliding into intersections, sliding into the backend of other vehicles etc etc...

It's going to happen to everyone and everything your instincts are going to tell you to do is going to lead you to trouble.

  1. Don't hit the brakes, locked up tires slide and lose control, rolling tires provide way more traction. If you need to slow down to stop then prepare ahead of time and lightly press the brake just until you feel friction then back off, and do that again a couple times light and slow, you want to slow the tires not stop them. so unless there is a vehicle or object directly in front of you just let off the gas.

  2. Turn into the slide not away from it, Lets say your turning left and the back end of the vehicle slides out to the right, you want to turn to the right until you feel it correct itself, then slow down and finish that left turn. If you turn left you're just putting more momentum into that backend rotation.

  3. Relax, Don't panic because if you panic you're likely to slam the brakes, and probably crank the wheel the wrong way, and even if you do manage to turn into the spin you're likely to overdo it and spin the other way.

Even stopping at intersections Don't hit the brake, plan your stop ahead of time and lightly pump the brake to slowly bring you to a controlled stop. locked up tires slide, rolling tires roll.

Good luck guys.

Also never underestimate good winter tires, I use studded tires and ven I slide all out all the time.
